rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created things praise God by their innate state, testifying to their Creator’s perfection and freedom from defect; people must also consciously glorify Him and avoid associating partners or imperfections with Him.
rows.anchor: Tesbih eder Allah’a (yahut Allah için) göklerdeki yerdeki hiçbir şey yoktur ki hâlıkının kemâline ve eksiklik şâibelerinden münezzeh olduğuna delâlet etmesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb conveys continual glorification, while its future orientation warns believers to persist in it after promised victory rather than become proud or follow Jews and Christians into excess.
rows.anchor: Burada يُسَبِّحُ fi‘l-i muzâri‘i[^1] zamandan münselih olarak istimrar içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is King because He creates, governs, and disposes the whole cosmic realm of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: bütün bu gökleri ve yerleriyle kainat mülkünü îcad ve tedbir ve tasarruf ile idare eden öyle bir hükümdar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddus means utterly pure: every perfection belongs to God, who exceeds all limits and accepts no partner, injustice, blemish, or need for child, friend, or helper.
rows.anchor: Kuddûs hiç lekesiz, tertemiz, pampâktir. Bütün temizlik, bütün medhe lâyık kemâlât, fezâil ve mehâsin O’nundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call in the preceding sūra to be God’s helpers does not mean God needs aid; humans need Him, and should continually sanctify Him.
rows.anchor: ihtiyâcı varmış gibi bir tevehhüme düşmemeli, ihtiyaç kendinizin olduğunu bilmeli

rows.speaker: حليمي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits al-Halimi’s account that explicit glorification entails sanctification and vice versa: denying defects affirms virtues, and affirming virtues denies defects.
rows.anchor: Beyhakī Esmâ ve Sıfât’ta “Kuddûs” isminin şerhinde Halîmî’den naklen der ki: “Kuddûs’un mânası fezâil ve mehâsin ile memduh demektir.

rows.speaker: حليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi says Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ combines sanctification in affirming God’s oneness and self-sufficiency with glorification in denying offspring and likeness; both affirm tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: İhlas Sûresi’nde ikisi cem‘olunmuştur. قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ takdistir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the preceding sūra, this opening glorification also rejects the Christian excess of the Trinity that arose after Christianity appeared.
rows.anchor: bu sûrenin böyle tesbih ve takdis ile başlaması Nasârâ’nın zuhûrundan sonra teslis davasıyla düştükleri gulüv ve ifrâtın ibtâline işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz denotes invincible majesty and power; God defeats and punishes those who attack His sanctity, violate His right, or associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: Azîz çok izzetli, kudsiyeti sarsılmaz, kudretine yetişilmez, ezelden muttasıf olduğu kuvvet ve azameti hiçbir suretle mağlup edilmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts with order and wisdom; apparent respite for wrongdoers lets truth and divine majesty be recognized, makes punishment deserved, and gives believers struggles through which their reward rises, since contrasts disclose things.
rows.anchor: Eşyânın zıtlarıyla inkişaf etmesi de bir kānûn-ı hikmettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummiyyin here means the Arabs. Ummī may mean one related to a mother and thus unlettered, one related to a community, or one from Mecca; Elmalılı prefers the famous first sense, confirmed by context.
rows.anchor: Meşhur olan evvelkidir. Burada sözün gidişinden de maksad o olduğu anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a hadith describing the community as unlettered, unable to write or calculate, as evidence for the first meaning of ummī.
rows.anchor: diye vârid olan bir hadiste bu mânaya işaret buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent from among the Arabs, then living in ignorance, a Messenger who became a source of knowledge and wisdom, as if bringing life out of the dead.
rows.anchor: ümmîler içinde kendilerinden bir Resul ba‘s buyurdu ki ümmîlerden murad Araplardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger recites God’s signs and purifies people from false beliefs and bad character, brings them spiritual flourishing, opens their minds, and makes them shine among peoples.
rows.anchor: Üzerlerine Allah’ın âyetlerini okuyor {وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ} ve onları tezkiye ediyor bâtıl akidelerden, fena huylardan temizleyip feyizlendiriyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the Book and wisdom includes literacy and instruction in the Qur’an, as well as the Sunnah and hadith and the transmitted and rational knowledge and practice needed to apply rulings.
rows.anchor: ve onlara kitap ve hikmet öğretiyor okuyup yazmayı ve kitapların en yükseği olan Kur’ân’ı belletiyor. Sünen ve ehâdîs ile icrâ-yı ahkâm için naklî ve aklî ilimler ve ameller tâlim eyliyor.

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Messenger came, the Arabs were in manifest error, bewildered and unsure what to do.
rows.anchor: bundan evvel o ümmîler açık bir dalâl içinde ne yapacaklarını bilmez şaşkın bir hâlde idiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase others of them is coordinated with ummiyyin, with them, or with the pronoun in teaches them; each construction extends the Messenger’s mission beyond the Arabs to later peoples.
rows.anchor: Bu “âharîn” “âhar”ın cem‘i olup ٱلْأُمِّيِّۦنَ’e veya عَلَيْهِمْ veya وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ’deki لِلَّهِ مَا zamirine ma‘tuf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger’s mission and teaching are universal: later Arabs and non-Arabs who had not yet joined the first audience are also included.
rows.anchor: ileride lâhık olacak olan Arap ve gayr-i Arap bütün insanlık âlemine kitap ve hikmet tâlim ediyor

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending this Messenger is pure divine grace, not something earned through effort or constrained by natural laws; God grants it to whom He wills, as an expression of His might and great bounty.
rows.anchor: İşte o ba‘s, öyle bir Resul gönderilmesi {فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ} Allah’ın mahz-ı fazlıdır kesb ile çalışmakla kazanılır bir şey değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should answer the Messenger, learn his instruction, and become helpers of God so they may attain the bounty and virtue promised through him.
rows.anchor: o Resûlünün davetine icâbet etmeli, ta‘lîmâtını bellemeli, ona göre ensârullah olup Allah’ın ona vaad buyurduğu fazl u fazilete ermelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given the Torah were taught it and charged to act on its contents, yet failed to understand, benefit from, or practice it; although learned and literate, they ignored its prophecies of the unlettered Prophet and did not live by its law and morals.
rows.anchor: öğretilip mazmûnuyla amel olunmak teklif olunmuş olup da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their likeness is a donkey carrying large books without knowing or benefiting from what is inside.
rows.anchor: o eşeğin hâline benzer ki {يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًۢا} sifrler, yani koca koca kitaplar taşır da içindekinden hiç haberi olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfar hints that the divisions of the Torah are themselves called books or volumes.
rows.anchor: aksâmına “esfâr” denildiğine işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ugly donkey simile warns that everyone who knows but does not act has a disgraceful likeness, while the verse particularly condemns those who deny God’s signs.
rows.anchor: bunda ilmiyle âmil olmayanların hepsinin de hâli, meseli böyle çirkin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide wrongdoers who, despite receiving proofs of truth, deny rather than affirm; such unjust people cannot reach the right path or their goal.
rows.anchor: Kendilerine hakkın delilleri gösterildiği hâlde onlara inanmayıp da tasdik yerine tekzîbi koyan haksızların

words: إِن زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı recalls the Jews’ claim to be God’s beloved friends and parallels the Christians’ claim to be God’s children and beloved, stated in 5:18.
rows.anchor: Yehûd da “biz Allah’ın sevgilileriyiz” diye iddia etmektedirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to wish for death is a challenge meant to corner and rebuke them: if they truly were God’s friends, they should long to leave worldly hardship and meet Him in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Burada mevti temenni emri ilzam ve tebkît içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their claim were true, they would welcome death instead of clinging to worldly life and avoiding it.
rows.anchor: Niçin ondan kaçıp da bütün mevcûdiyetinizle dünyâ hayata sarılıp duruyorsunuz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will never wish for death because of the many sins, crimes, acts of unbelief, and injustices they have committed; such people cannot be God’s beloved friends.
rows.anchor: Çünkü ellerinin takdim eylediği nice günahlar, cinayetler, küfürler, zulümler var ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows and will punish wrongdoers; therefore they are liars in claiming to be His friends and are unjust rather than beloved.
rows.anchor: Ve Allah zâlimleri bilir cezâlarını verir. Onun için onlar o davada sâdık değil, kâzibdirler; evliyâ değil, haksız zâlimlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabat and nabt can be a collective noun for anything growing from the earth, conventionally especially grass or fodder, or a verbal noun meaning sprouting and growing; anbata means to make grow or bring forth.
rows.anchor: İsim olduğuna göre yerde biten, yani neş’et edip yetişen her şeye denir, sonra sâkı olmayanda belki hayvânâtın yediğinde örf olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Growth is the distinguishing feature of vegetation, manifested through nourishment and reproduction.
rows.anchor: Nebâtın faslı, mümeyyiz[^1] vasfı nümüvdür ki uzviyetin tegaddî ve tenasül ile

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators take nabatan as a cognate accusative rather than a circumstantial accusative because it is originally a verbal noun and human life is not simply plant life.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn burada أَنۢبَتَكُم hâl değil, masdar olarak mef‘ûl-i mutlak olduğunu beyan[^2]

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation treats nabatan directly as the cognate accusative of anbata, with the sense that God raised you by growing you from the earth.
rows.anchor: Ancak bazıları doğrudan doğru أَنۢبَتَكُم’den mef‘ûl-i mutlak olmak için

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another explanation makes nabatan the resultative verbal noun of an implied triliteral verb: God caused you to grow, and you grew a growth.
rows.anchor: neticesi olmak üzere sülâsî bâbından mukadder olan fiilin masdarı olmak dolayısıyla

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi gives two senses: God first created humanity through Adam from soil, as in 3:59, or created all people from the earth through seed, food, and plants that ultimately come from earth.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Bunda iki mesele vardır. Birincisi: Âyette iki vecih var: birisi, ‘sizi Arz’dan bitirdi’ demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı endorses the point that the unusual wording makes human growth directly observable, allowing it to serve as evidence of God’s perfect power rather than requiring reliance only on revelation.
rows.anchor: İkincisi اَنـْبَتَكُمْ إنـْبَاتًا denilmek gerekken اَنـْبَتَكُمْ نـَبَاتًا buyurulmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if nabatan is taken as a circumstantial phrase the nuance remains, but commentators prefer its basic verbal-noun sense as a cognate accusative, which is prior and stronger than the circumstantial construction.
rows.anchor: kelimenin esasen masdar olması ve mef‘ûl-i mutlakın hâlden akdem ve daha kuvvetli bulunması hasebiyle müfessirîn hâlden ziyade esası gözetmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After indicating the beginnings of human stages, the passage turns to their future and end: return to the earth and subsequent emergence from it.
rows.anchor: etvârın mebâdîsine işaretten sonra istikbâlini ve gayesini beyan için de buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is agreement that this verse came later than the opening night-vigil command and softened or adjusted it; scholars differ about whether it was revealed in Mecca or Medina and how the easing or abrogation worked.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin sonradan nâzil olup sûrenin evvelindeki kıyâm-ı leyl emrini tahfif ve ta‘dîl etmiş olduğunda ittifak vardır. Ancak yine Mekke’de mi yoksa sonradan Medine’de mi nâzil olduğunda

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from Aisha says the verse came eight months after the opening command, restored the originally near-obligatory night vigil to its basic prescribed amount, abrogated the extra burden, and left the excess voluntary.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den bu âyetin يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ’den sekiz ay sonra nâzil olup baştan farîza gibi yazılmış olan kıyâm-ı leyli

words: عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the original vigil was very burdensome and believers kept it like their Ramadan vigil; God then eased it through the clause commanding them to recite what was manageable, graciously widening rather than narrowing the duty, about a year later.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan da: “Müzzemmil’in evvelindeki إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the believers kept night vigil for one or two years after the opening command, until their feet and legs swelled; the command to recite what was easy then brought them relief.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den: “يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ nâzil oldu, bir sene veya iki sene kıyam ettiler

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reports that Muslims kept night vigil for a year, with some able to do so and others unable, until the concession came; after an obligation, the vigil became voluntary worship.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan: “يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ âyeti nâzil olunca müslimler

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa‘id reports that the Prophet and a group of companions continued the commanded vigil for ten years, until this passage was revealed and lightened the duty.
rows.anchor: Abd b. Humeyd’in, Ya‘kūb, Ca‘fer tarîkiyle[^10] Sa‘îd’den rivayetinde

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Some scholars call the verse Medinan; Abu Hayyan describes that as the majority position, but Elmalılı says it does not appear to be the majority view.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân buna “cumhur kavli” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinan dating is sometimes inferred from the zakat command; Elmalılı replies that Medina fixed zakat’s recipients and shares, not zakat’s basic obligation, since Meccan sūras also mention it.
rows.anchor: Medine’de farz kılınan asl-ı[^13] zekât olmayıp Sûre-i Berâe âyeti mûcebince masriflerin, nasiblerin tâyini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı considers the mention of fighting a clearer sign that at least one or two clauses are Medinan: permission to fight was agreed to be Medinan, and even the prediction of fighters preparatorily signals that permission and its abrogating circumstances.
rows.anchor: Bizim kanaatimizce bu âyetin Medenî [5439] olduğunu andıran bir karîne daha vardır; وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ fıkrasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because no other Meccan verse explicitly mentions fighting, this clue seems clearer than zakat; Elmalılı concludes that at least some sentences of the verse must be Medinan, even if not the whole verse.
rows.anchor: buradan başka Mekkî bir âyette kıtalden sarâhaten bahsedilmemiş bulunmasına nazaran bunun Medenî olması bize zekât fıkrasından daha vâzıh görünüyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reduces the severity and amount of the opening night-vigil duty; after the five daily prayers became obligatory, evening and night prayers remained within the night vigil, while tahajjud changed from obligatory to recommended.
rows.anchor: bu âyet sûrenin başındaki gece kıyâmı emrinin şiddetini, mikdârını tahfif etmiş, beş vakit namaz farz kılındıktan sonra akşam, yatsı gece kıyâmı cümlesinden kalarak teheccüdün[^14] vücûbu nedbe tehavvül eylemiştir.

words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported vigil durations indicate a maximum slightly under two thirds of the night, a middle amount of one half, and a minimum of one third.
rows.anchor: demek ki a‘zamî kıyam müddeti sülüsândan biraz eksik (اَوْ زِدْ), vasatîsi nısf[^15], asgarîsi (اَوِ انْقُصْ) sülüs[^16] oluyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reading under discussion, wa-nisfahu and wa-thuluthahu are accusative and coordinated with adna.
rows.anchor: Bu kıraatte وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ mansub olarak أَدْنَىٰ üzerine ma‘tuftur.
